topic: DACA Recipient Health Insurance Options 2026 After Federal Marketplace Exclusion

title.es: Opciones de Seguro Médico DACA 2026 | CoveredUSA

description.en: DACA recipients cannot use the ACA Marketplace as of August 2025. Compare employer plans, FQHCs, and state-funded options still available in 2026.
description.es: Receptores de DACA no pueden usar el Mercado ACA desde agosto 2025. Compare planes del empleador, centros de salud comunitaria y opciones estatales en 2026.

h1.en: DACA Recipient? Here Are Your Real Health Insurance Options for 2026
h1.es: ¿Receptor de DACA? Aquí Están Sus Opciones Reales de Seguro Médico para 2026

subhero.en: Federal rules removed DACA recipients from ACA Marketplace eligibility effective August 2025. Employer plans, Federally Qualified Health Centers, and several state-funded programs remain open. The right path depends on your income, state, and employer.
subhero.es: Las reglas federales removieron a los receptores de DACA de elegibilidad del Mercado ACA desde agosto 2025. Planes del empleador, centros de salud comunitaria federalmente calificados y varios programas estatales siguen abiertos.

heading.en: No single federal enrollment deadline applies now, but state and employer windows matter
heading.es: No hay una fecha límite federal única ahora, pero las ventanas estatales y del empleador importan

body.en: DACA recipients lost federal Marketplace coverage eligibility permanently effective August 25, 2025. Federally Qualified Health Centers enroll year-round. Employer plan open enrollment windows vary by employer. Several state-funded programs, including New Mexico's DACA-specific plan and Washington Healthplanfinder with state subsidies, have their own enrollment periods. Check your state's program directly.
body.es: Los receptores de DACA perdieron la elegibilidad para el Mercado federal permanentemente desde el 25 de agosto de 2025. Los centros de salud comunitaria inscriben durante todo el año. Las ventanas de inscripción de planes del empleador varían. Varios programas estatales tienen sus propios períodos de inscripción.

label.es: Ventana de evento calificador del plan del empleador
Centro de salud comunitaria FQHC (todo el año)

quickAnswer.en: DACA recipients cannot enroll in ACA Marketplace plans or receive Premium Tax Credits as of August 25, 2025, following a final federal rule. Federal Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare are also unavailable. Your four remaining paths in 2026 are: (1) employer-sponsored health insurance if your job offers it, (2) off-Marketplace direct purchase from an insurer with no subsidy, (3) Federally Qualified Health Centers providing sliding-scale care regardless of insurance status, and (4) state-funded programs available in California (Medi-Cal for those enrolled before Jan 1, 2026), New York, New Mexico, Washington, and Colorado. The DACA legal status itself remains separately contested in federal courts, which does not affect the health insurance rule.
quickAnswer.es: Los receptores de DACA no pueden inscribirse en planes del Mercado ACA ni recibir Créditos Fiscales de Prima desde el 25 de agosto de 2025, según una regla federal final. Medicaid federal, CHIP y Medicare tampoco están disponibles. Sus cuatro caminos restantes en 2026 son: (1) seguro médico del empleador si su trabajo lo ofrece, (2) compra directa fuera del Mercado sin subsidio, (3) centros de salud comunitaria federalmente calificados con escala de tarifas según ingreso, y (4) programas estatales en California, Nueva York, Nuevo México, Washington y Colorado.

introParagraphs.en: DACA recipients faced a major coverage disruption in 2025 when the Trump administration finalized a rule in June 2025, effective August 25, 2025, removing DACA from the definition of 'lawfully present' for purposes of ACA Marketplace eligibility, Premium Tax Credits, cost-sharing reductions, and the Basic Health Program. An estimated 10,000 to 11,000 DACA recipients who had been enrolled in Marketplace plans or Basic Health Program coverage lost that coverage on September 30, 2025. This was a direct reversal of a Biden-era final rule from November 2024 that had included DACA recipients in Marketplace eligibility. The 2025 rule change is permanent, meaning there is no current sunset or scheduled reversal. DACA recipients remain federally ineligible for Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare under both the 2025 rule and the original Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act (PRWORA) framework that has governed immigrant benefit eligibility since 1996.
introParagraphs.es: Los receptores de DACA enfrentaron una interrupción importante de cobertura en 2025 cuando la administración Trump finalizó una regla en junio de 2025, vigente desde el 25 de agosto de 2025, removiendo a DACA de la definición de 'legalmente presente' para propósitos de elegibilidad del Mercado ACA, Créditos Fiscales de Prima, reducciones de costos compartidos y el Programa Básico de Salud. Aproximadamente 10,000 a 11,000 receptores de DACA que estaban inscritos en planes del Mercado o cobertura del Programa Básico de Salud perdieron esa cobertura el 30 de septiembre de 2025. Este fue un cambio directo de la era Biden que había incluido a los receptores de DACA en la elegibilidad del Mercado en noviembre de 2024.

introParagraphs.en: Losing Marketplace access does not mean losing all paths to health coverage. Several options remain available in 2026. Employer-sponsored insurance remains the most common path for DACA recipients who are working, since private employers can offer group health plans to any employee regardless of immigration status and work authorization category. Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) provide primary care, dental, behavioral health, and preventive services on a sliding-fee-scale basis to anyone regardless of insurance status or immigration status, as guaranteed under 42 U.S.C. Section 254b. Multiple states have used state funding, Section 1332 waivers, or state-law programs to extend some form of coverage to DACA recipients outside the federal Marketplace framework. Understanding which option fits your state, income, and employment situation is the critical first step for DACA recipients navigating coverage in 2026. Check your options through healthcare.gov for immigration status guidance and your state Medicaid agency for state-funded programs.
introParagraphs.es: Perder el acceso al Mercado no significa perder todos los caminos hacia cobertura de salud. Varias opciones permanecen disponibles en 2026. El seguro médico del empleador sigue siendo el camino más común para los receptores de DACA que trabajan, ya que los empleadores privados pueden ofrecer planes de salud grupales a cualquier empleado independientemente del estatus migratorio. Los Centros de Salud Comunitaria Federalmente Calificados (FQHC) brindan atención primaria, dental, salud conductual y servicios preventivos en una escala de tarifas según ingreso a cualquier persona, independientemente del estatus de seguro o migratorio, bajo 42 U.S.C. Sección 254b. Múltiples estados han utilizado fondos estatales, exenciones de la Sección 1332 o programas estatales para extender alguna forma de cobertura a los receptores de DACA fuera del marco federal del Mercado.

name.en: Confirm your current coverage status and state
name.es: Confirme su estado de cobertura actual y su estado

text.en: Check whether you are in a state with its own DACA-coverage program: California (Medi-Cal if enrolled before Jan 1, 2026), New Mexico (state-funded plan via hca.nm.gov), Washington (state-subsidized Marketplace via wahbexchange.org), New York (state-funded Essential Plan), or Colorado (OmniSalud via connectforhealthco.com). Log in to your current insurer or Marketplace account to verify whether your coverage was terminated as of October 1, 2025.
text.es: Verifique si está en un estado con su propio programa de cobertura para DACA: California (Medi-Cal si se inscribió antes del 1 de enero de 2026), Nuevo México (plan estatal), Washington (Mercado con subsidio estatal), Nueva York (Plan Esencial con fondos estatales) o Colorado (OmniSalud). Inicie sesión en su aseguradora actual o cuenta del Mercado para verificar si su cobertura terminó el 1 de octubre de 2025.

name.en: Apply for employer-sponsored coverage if your job offers it
name.es: Solicite cobertura del empleador si su trabajo la ofrece

text.en: Losing Marketplace coverage on October 1, 2025 was a qualifying life event for most employer plans, triggering a 30-day special enrollment window. If you missed that window, apply during your employer's next annual open enrollment. Call your HR department or benefits administrator and ask specifically about the 30-day qualifying event window. Many employers running calendar-year plans open enrollment in October or November each year for January 1 coverage.
text.es: Perder la cobertura del Mercado el 1 de octubre de 2025 fue un evento calificador de vida para la mayoría de los planes del empleador, activando una ventana de inscripción especial de 30 días. Si perdió esa ventana, solicite durante la próxima inscripción abierta anual de su empleador. Llame a Recursos Humanos y pregunte específicamente sobre la ventana de 30 días para eventos calificadores.

name.en: Find a Federally Qualified Health Center near you
name.es: Encuentre un Centro de Salud Comunitaria Federalmente Calificado cerca

text.en: Use the HRSA Find a Health Center tool at findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov to locate FQHCs near you. FQHCs are federally funded community health centers required by law to serve all patients on a sliding-fee-scale regardless of insurance or immigration status. Most offer primary care, prenatal care, dental, behavioral health, and pharmacy services. Fees are calculated as a percentage of income, often $20 to $100 per visit for uninsured patients. No one can be turned away for inability to pay under 42 U.S.C. Section 254b.
text.es: Use la herramienta de búsqueda HRSA en findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov para localizar centros FQHC cerca de usted. Los FQHC son centros de salud comunitaria con fondos federales que por ley deben atender a todos los pacientes en una escala de tarifas según ingreso, independientemente del seguro o estatus migratorio. La mayoría ofrece atención primaria, prenatal, dental, salud conductual y servicios de farmacia. Las tarifas se calculan como porcentaje del ingreso.

name.es: Explore planes de compra directa fuera del Mercado

text.en: DACA recipients can purchase health insurance directly from private insurance companies outside of the Marketplace without federal subsidies. Contact major insurers such as Blue Cross Blue Shield, Aetna, or UnitedHealthcare directly to compare off-Exchange qualified health plans. These plans cover the same essential health benefits as Marketplace plans but cost full premium with no Premium Tax Credit. For a single adult, expect $350 to $700 per month in 2026 depending on age, plan tier, and location. Compare plans at each insurer's website directly.
text.es: Los receptores de DACA pueden comprar seguro médico directamente de compañías de seguros privadas fuera del Mercado sin subsidios federales. Contacte directamente a aseguradoras principales como Blue Cross Blue Shield, Aetna o UnitedHealthcare para comparar planes calificados fuera del Mercado. Estos planes cubren los mismos beneficios esenciales de salud pero cuestan la prima completa sin Crédito Fiscal. Para un adulto individual, espere $350 a $700 al mes en 2026.

name.en: If in California, check Medi-Cal eligibility and enrollment status
name.es: Si está en California, verifique elegibilidad e inscripción en Medi-Cal

text.en: California's Medi-Cal program has covered DACA recipients since the creation of DACA through state law. However, new Medi-Cal enrollment for undocumented immigrants and DACA recipients age 19 and older was frozen as of January 1, 2026, due to California budget constraints. DACA recipients already enrolled in Medi-Cal before January 1, 2026 can maintain their coverage. If you are not enrolled, check your county social services office or apply at coveredca.com to verify current eligibility rules that may have changed after January 1, 2026.
text.es: El programa Medi-Cal de California ha cubierto a los receptores de DACA desde la creación del programa a través de la ley estatal. Sin embargo, la nueva inscripción en Medi-Cal para inmigrantes indocumentados y receptores de DACA de 19 años o más fue congelada desde el 1 de enero de 2026 por restricciones presupuestarias. Los receptores de DACA ya inscritos antes del 1 de enero de 2026 pueden mantener su cobertura.

name.en: If in New Mexico, apply through the state DACA coverage plan
name.es: Si está en Nuevo México, solicite el plan estatal de cobertura DACA

text.en: New Mexico has one of the most direct DACA-specific coverage programs in the country. The New Mexico Health Care Authority offers state-funded premium assistance on a sliding scale based on household income and county. Apply at hca.nm.gov/daca-coverage and compare the Clear Cost Gold Plan offered through this program. Premium assistance reduces costs based on your income relative to the 2026 Federal Poverty Level guidelines published by HHS ASPE.
text.es: Nuevo México tiene uno de los programas de cobertura específica para DACA más directos del país. La Autoridad de Cuidado de Salud de Nuevo México ofrece asistencia premium estatal en escala deslizante según ingreso del hogar y condado. Solicite en hca.nm.gov/daca-coverage y compare el Plan Clear Cost Gold ofrecido a través de este programa.

name.en: Check for a qualifying life event if employer coverage or state programs become available
name.es: Verifique si hay un evento calificador de vida si hay cobertura del empleador o programas estatales disponibles

text.en: Future qualifying life events such as starting a new job with benefits, getting married to someone with employer coverage, or a state program changing its rules can trigger a new 30-day or 60-day enrollment window for employer plans. Document the date of each qualifying event. Contact your employer HR department immediately when a qualifying event occurs and request the Special Enrollment Period form in writing. Keep copies of all enrollment documents for tax purposes and to prove continuous coverage if seeking COBRA continuation from an employer plan later.
text.es: Eventos calificadores de vida futuros como comenzar un nuevo trabajo con beneficios, casarse con alguien con cobertura del empleador, o un programa estatal cambiando sus reglas pueden activar una nueva ventana de inscripción de 30 o 60 días para planes del empleador. Documente la fecha de cada evento calificador. Contacte a RR.HH. del empleador inmediatamente cuando ocurra un evento calificador.

footnote.en: Federal Marketplace plans, Premium Tax Credits, Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare are unavailable to DACA recipients under the 2025 federal rule. State programs change; verify current enrollment status with your state agency before applying. Off-Marketplace direct purchase costs are estimated for a single adult; family and age-adjusted rates vary significantly.
footnote.es: Los planes federales del Mercado, los Créditos Fiscales de Prima, Medicaid, CHIP y Medicare no están disponibles para receptores de DACA bajo la regla federal de 2025. Los programas estatales cambian; verifique el estado actual de inscripción con su agencia estatal antes de solicitar.

intro.en: The most costly mistakes DACA recipients make when navigating health coverage in 2026:
intro.es: Los errores más costosos que los receptores de DACA cometen al buscar cobertura de salud en 2026:

items.en: Attempting to enroll through HealthCare.gov without checking current DACA eligibility. DACA recipients are permanently excluded from federal Marketplace plans and Premium Tax Credits as of August 25, 2025. Attempting to enroll may result in coverage cancellation and potential repayment of any subsidies.
items.es: Intentar inscribirse en HealthCare.gov sin verificar elegibilidad DACA actual. Los receptores de DACA están permanentemente excluidos del Mercado federal desde el 25 de agosto de 2025. Intentar inscribirse puede resultar en cancelación de cobertura y posible reembolso de subsidios.

items.en: Assuming all states have DACA-specific programs. State-funded DACA health programs exist only in a handful of states including California, New Mexico, Washington, and New York. Residents of the 40 or so other states without such programs must rely on employer coverage or off-Marketplace direct purchase.
items.es: Asumir que todos los estados tienen programas específicos para DACA. Los programas estatales de salud para DACA existen solo en un puñado de estados como California, Nuevo México, Washington y Nueva York. Los residentes de los otros estados sin tales programas deben depender de cobertura del empleador o compra directa.

items.en: Missing the 30-day employer plan qualifying event window. When DACA recipients lost Marketplace coverage on October 1, 2025, that triggered a qualifying life event for employer plans at most companies. Missing this window meant waiting until the next annual open enrollment, often November or December.
items.es: Perder la ventana de 30 días del evento calificador del plan del empleador. Cuando los receptores de DACA perdieron la cobertura del Mercado el 1 de octubre de 2025, eso activó un evento calificador de vida para los planes del empleador. Perder esta ventana significó esperar hasta la próxima inscripción abierta anual.

items.en: Confusing DACA litigation status with health insurance eligibility. Federal courts are still litigating the broader DACA program, but that litigation does not affect the health insurance rule. The 2025 Marketplace exclusion is a separate administrative rule and remains in effect regardless of DACA's overall legal status.
items.es: Confundir el estado de litigación de DACA con la elegibilidad de seguro médico. Los tribunales federales todavía están litigando el programa DACA, pero esa litigación no afecta la regla de seguro médico. La exclusión del Mercado de 2025 es una regla administrativa separada y permanece vigente.

items.en: Skipping Federally Qualified Health Centers. DACA recipients who are uninsured often delay care because they cannot afford private coverage. FQHCs provide primary care, prescriptions, dental, and behavioral health on a sliding-scale that starts at near-$0 for very low-income patients. Use findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov to find one near you.
items.es: Omitir los Centros de Salud Comunitaria Federalmente Calificados. Los receptores de DACA sin seguro a menudo retrasan la atención porque no pueden pagar cobertura privada. Los FQHC brindan atención primaria, recetas, dental y salud conductual en una escala que comienza en casi $0 para pacientes de muy bajos ingresos.

items.en: Not checking the California Medi-Cal enrollment freeze date. DACA recipients in California who were enrolled in Medi-Cal before January 1, 2026 can maintain coverage. Those not enrolled by that date cannot newly enroll. Many missed this critical cutoff by not knowing about it early enough.
items.es: No verificar la fecha de congelamiento de inscripción de Medi-Cal en California. Los receptores de DACA en California inscritos en Medi-Cal antes del 1 de enero de 2026 pueden mantener cobertura. Los que no se inscribieron antes no pueden inscribirse nuevamente. Muchos perdieron este plazo crítico.

heading.en: Employer Plans vs. Off-Marketplace Direct Purchase vs. State Programs: Which Should You Choose?
heading.es: Planes del Empleador vs. Compra Directa vs. Programas Estatales: ¿Cuál Debe Elegir?

paragraphs.en: Employer-sponsored coverage is the strongest option for DACA recipients in 2026 for one decisive reason: cost-sharing. Employers typically pay 70 to 80 percent of the total premium for employee-only coverage and 40 to 60 percent for family coverage. For a full-time worker, that can mean $50 to $200 per month out-of-pocket for comprehensive coverage that would cost $350 to $700 per month if purchased directly. No immigration status requirement applies to private employer group health plans. Federal non-discrimination employment law that applies to DACA recipients through their Employment Authorization Document (EAD) means they have equal access to employer benefits. If your employer offers coverage, enroll at the next available window.
paragraphs.es: La cobertura del empleador es la opción más sólida para los receptores de DACA en 2026 por una razón decisiva: el reparto de costos. Los empleadores típicamente pagan el 70 a 80 por ciento de la prima total para cobertura solo del empleado. Para un trabajador a tiempo completo, eso puede significar $50 a $200 al mes por cobertura integral que costaría $350 a $700 al mes si se comprara directamente. No se aplica ningún requisito de estatus migratorio a los planes grupales del empleador privado.

paragraphs.en: Off-Marketplace direct purchase is the backup path when employer coverage is unavailable. Qualified Health Plans purchased outside the Exchange cover the same essential health benefits, including preventive services, hospitalization, prescription drugs, and mental health, that Marketplace plans do. The critical difference is cost: without a Premium Tax Credit, a Silver plan for a 35-year-old in 2026 typically runs $450 to $600 per month depending on geography. Contact major insurers directly, such as Blue Cross Blue Shield, Aetna, UnitedHealthcare, or Cigna. State-funded programs in New Mexico, Washington, Colorado, and New York may dramatically lower that cost if you are a resident. New Mexico's state program at hca.nm.gov/daca-coverage offers the clearest DACA-specific application pathway in 2026.
paragraphs.es: La compra directa fuera del Mercado es el camino de respaldo cuando la cobertura del empleador no está disponible. Los Planes de Salud Calificados comprados fuera del Mercado cubren los mismos beneficios esenciales. La diferencia crítica es el costo: sin un Crédito Fiscal de Prima, un plan Silver para un adulto de 35 años en 2026 típicamente cuesta $450 a $600 al mes. Los programas estatales en Nuevo México, Washington, Colorado y Nueva York pueden reducir drásticamente ese costo.

heading.es: Programas de Cobertura DACA por Estado en 2026

paragraphs.en: State programs for DACA health coverage vary significantly and are subject to legislative and budget changes. California's Medi-Cal program covered DACA recipients under state law since 2014. As of January 1, 2026, new enrollment for adults age 19 and older who are not pregnant or former foster youth has been frozen due to state budget constraints. DACA recipients already enrolled before that date can continue their coverage. Medi-Cal remains free for income-eligible enrollees and covers comprehensive benefits. Check coveredca.com or your county social services office for current eligibility rules. New York allows state-funded enrollment in the Essential Plan for income-eligible DACA recipients under the governor's proposed 2026-27 budget using state funds to replace lost federal subsidies. Verify current status at nystateofhealth.ny.gov. Washington state obtained a Section 1332 waiver that allows undocumented individuals to enroll through Washington Healthplanfinder, and the state provides premium assistance that can substitute for federal Premium Tax Credits for DACA recipients. Apply at wahbexchange.org. Colorado operates OmniSalud through a Section 1332 waiver using connectforhealthco.com, though state funding for premium assistance is significantly reduced in 2026. New Mexico provides the most direct DACA-specific state program: a clear application path at hca.nm.gov/daca-coverage with income-based sliding scale premium assistance for a Clear Cost Gold Plan.
paragraphs.es: Los programas estatales para cobertura de salud DACA varían significativamente y están sujetos a cambios legislativos y presupuestarios. California, Nueva York, Washington, Colorado y Nuevo México tienen los programas más destacados. California congeló nuevas inscripciones para adultos de 19 años o más desde el 1 de enero de 2026 por restricciones presupuestarias, aunque los inscritos antes pueden continuar. Nuevo México tiene el camino de solicitud más claro en hca.nm.gov/daca-coverage con asistencia premium según ingreso. Verifique el estado actual de cada programa con la agencia estatal relevante.

list.es: California: Medi-Cal para inscritos existentes (inscritos antes del 1 de enero de 2026); nueva inscripción congelada para adultos 19+ desde enero 2026

heading.en: Federally Qualified Health Centers: Year-Round Primary Care for the Uninsured
heading.es: Centros de Salud Comunitaria Federalmente Calificados: Atención Primaria Todo el Año para No Asegurados

paragraphs.en: Federally Qualified Health Centers are a critical safety net for DACA recipients who cannot access any insurance program. FQHCs receive federal grants under the Health Center Program (42 U.S.C. Section 254b) and are legally required to serve all patients regardless of ability to pay, insurance status, or immigration status. More than 1,400 FQHC organizations operate over 15,000 service sites across all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and the US territories. Services typically include: adult and pediatric primary care, OB/GYN and prenatal care, dental care, behavioral health counseling, HIV care, substance use disorder treatment, and pharmacy services at reduced prices. Fees are set on a sliding scale based on household income as a percentage of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level guidelines. Patients with income at or below 100 percent of FPL, which is $15,960 for a single person or $33,000 for a family of four in 2026, typically pay the lowest sliding-scale fees, often $20 to $40 per visit. Use findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov to search by ZIP code. FQHCs do not replace hospitalization coverage or specialist care, but they cover the vast majority of routine and preventive health needs at dramatically reduced cost.
paragraphs.es: Los Centros de Salud Comunitaria Federalmente Calificados son una red de seguridad crítica para los receptores de DACA que no pueden acceder a ningún programa de seguro. Los FQHC reciben subvenciones federales bajo el Programa de Centros de Salud (42 U.S.C. Sección 254b) y están legalmente obligados a atender a todos los pacientes independientemente de la capacidad de pago, estatus de seguro o estatus migratorio. Los servicios incluyen atención primaria para adultos y niños, atención prenatal, dental, salud conductual, farmacia a precios reducidos y más. Las tarifas se establecen en una escala según ingreso del hogar como porcentaje del nivel de pobreza federal de 2026. Los pacientes con ingresos en o por debajo del 100 por ciento del FPL, que es $15,960 para una persona o $33,000 para familia de cuatro en 2026, típicamente pagan las tarifas más bajas.

heading.en: Documents Needed to Prove DACA Status and Enroll in Available Programs
heading.es: Documentos Necesarios para Probar Estatus DACA e Inscribirse en Programas Disponibles

paragraphs.en: Enrollment in employer plans, off-Marketplace plans, and state-funded programs each requires specific documentation. Gathering these in advance significantly reduces processing time and the risk of enrollment gaps. Employer plan enrollment typically requires your DACA Employment Authorization Document (EAD card), Social Security number, proof of address, and date of birth. State programs vary: New Mexico's program requires DACA status documentation, proof of New Mexico residency, income documentation, and household composition information. FQHC sliding-scale enrollment requires proof of income such as recent pay stubs, tax returns, or unemployment award letters, and identification such as an EAD card. No immigration documentation beyond DACA EAD is typically required at FQHCs for access to care. Keep copies of all DACA renewal notices, EAD cards, and any coverage termination letters from your prior Marketplace insurer. Coverage termination letters from October 2025 are proof of prior coverage loss and may be needed if you later need to demonstrate a qualifying life event for a new employer plan.
paragraphs.es: La inscripción en planes del empleador, planes fuera del Mercado y programas estatales requiere documentación específica. Reunirla con anticipación reduce significativamente el tiempo de procesamiento. La inscripción en el plan del empleador típicamente requiere su Documento de Autorización de Empleo (tarjeta EAD) de DACA, número de Seguro Social, comprobante de dirección y fecha de nacimiento. Los FQHC requieren comprobante de ingresos para la escala de tarifas, como talones de pago recientes. Guarde copias de todos los avisos de renovación de DACA, tarjetas EAD y cartas de terminación de cobertura de su aseguradora anterior del Mercado.

en.footnote: Alaska and Hawaii have higher FPL thresholds. FQHC sliding-scale fees are set by each health center individually based on HHS poverty guidelines. State programs set their own income limits using these FPL percentages as benchmarks.

es.footnote: Alaska y Hawaii tienen umbrales FPL más altos. Las tarifas de escala deslizante FQHC las establece cada centro individualmente basado en las pautas de pobreza de HHS. Los programas estatales establecen sus propios límites de ingreso usando estos porcentajes FPL como referencia.
es.source: Directrices de Pobreza HHS ASPE 2026 + requisitos del Programa de Centros de Salud HRSA

en: DACA Employment Authorization Document (EAD card) as primary identity and status proof
Social Security number (required for employer plan enrollment and state program applications)
Proof of address (utility bill, lease agreement, or bank statement showing current address and state)
Recent pay stubs (last 2-4 weeks) or most recent tax return for income verification for FQHC sliding scale or state programs
Coverage termination letter from your former Marketplace insurer (dated October 2025 or whenever your coverage ended; documents qualifying life event for employer plans)
Birth certificates for dependents if adding children to employer coverage or state program
DACA approval notice (I-797 Notice of Action) as backup documentation if EAD card is under renewal
es: Documento de Autorización de Empleo (tarjeta EAD) de DACA como prueba primaria de identidad y estatus
Número de Seguro Social (requerido para inscripción en plan del empleador y solicitudes de programas estatales)
Comprobante de domicilio (factura de servicios, contrato de arrendamiento o estado de cuenta bancario)
Talones de pago recientes (últimas 2-4 semanas) o declaración de impuestos más reciente para verificación de ingreso
Carta de terminación de cobertura de su antigua aseguradora del Mercado (fechada en octubre de 2025 o cuando terminó su cobertura)
Actas de nacimiento para dependientes si agrega hijos a cobertura del empleador o programa estatal
Aviso de aprobación de DACA (Aviso de Acción I-797) como documentación de respaldo si la tarjeta EAD está en renovación

stateRules.rule: Medi-Cal covers DACA recipients under state law. New enrollment for adults age 19 and older frozen as of January 1, 2026, due to state budget. Existing enrollees maintain coverage. Dental benefits for DACA adults reduced as of July 2026.
State-funded DACA-specific health coverage program via HCA. Income-based sliding scale premium assistance for Clear Cost Gold Plan. Dedicated enrollment portal at hca.nm.gov/daca-coverage.

Washington Healthplanfinder allows enrollment for undocumented and DACA recipients under a Section 1332 waiver. State-funded premium assistance available but DACA recipients no longer eligible for federal Premium Tax Credits as of August 2025.

Governor proposed state funds to cover income-eligible DACA recipients losing Essential Plan federal eligibility. Verify current legislative status at nystateofhealth.ny.gov. DACA recipients were eligible for Essential Plan under state funding through mid-2026.

OmniSalud program via Connect for Health Colorado allows enrollment under Section 1332 waiver. State-funded premium assistance reduced significantly in 2026 budget. Verify current availability at connectforhealthco.com.

en: Attempting to enroll in a federal Marketplace plan: DACA recipients are permanently excluded from HealthCare.gov and state Exchanges using federal funds as of August 25, 2025. Applications are denied and previous subsidies may need to be repaid.

Missing the 30-day employer qualifying event window: Coverage termination on October 1, 2025 triggered a limited enrollment window. Most employers require written documentation of the qualifying event within 30 days and will not accept late enrollments outside of annual open enrollment.

Insufficient income documentation for FQHC sliding scale: FQHCs require at minimum recent pay stubs or a self-declaration of income to set the fee tier. Arriving without documentation may result in being charged full-fee until the paperwork is completed.

Incomplete DACA status documentation for state programs: State programs such as New Mexico's require active DACA status documentation (current EAD card or I-797 approval notice). Expired EAD cards without renewal documentation will delay or deny enrollment.

Applying to a state program as a non-resident: State-funded DACA programs are available only to residents of that specific state. Providing an out-of-state address will result in automatic denial regardless of DACA status.
es: Intentar inscribirse en un plan federal del Mercado: Los receptores de DACA están permanentemente excluidos de HealthCare.gov y Mercados estatales que usan fondos federales desde el 25 de agosto de 2025. Las solicitudes se niegan y es posible que haya que reembolsar subsidios anteriores.

Perder la ventana de 30 días del evento calificador del empleador: La terminación de cobertura el 1 de octubre de 2025 activó una ventana de inscripción limitada. La mayoría de los empleadores requieren documentación escrita del evento calificador dentro de los 30 días.

Documentación de ingreso insuficiente para la escala de tarifas FQHC: Los FQHC requieren al mínimo talones de pago recientes o autodeclaración de ingreso para establecer el nivel de tarifa. Llegar sin documentación puede resultar en tarifa completa.

Documentación de estatus DACA incompleta para programas estatales: Los programas estatales como el de Nuevo México requieren documentación de estatus DACA activo (tarjeta EAD vigente o aviso de aprobación I-797).

Solicitar un programa estatal sin ser residente de ese estado: Los programas DACA financiados por el estado solo están disponibles para residentes de ese estado específico. Proporcionar una dirección fuera del estado resultará en negación automática.

heading.en: Employer Plan vs. Off-Marketplace Purchase vs. State Program vs. FQHC: Decision Matrix for 2026
heading.es: Plan del Empleador vs. Compra Fuera del Mercado vs. Programa Estatal vs. FQHC: Matriz de Decisión 2026

body.en: DACA recipients in 2026 have four coverage pathways, each with a dramatically different cost profile. Employer-sponsored plans are the strongest option: if your employer offers group health insurance, enroll immediately. Employers typically cover 70 to 80 percent of the premium for employee-only coverage, making out-of-pocket costs $50 to $200 per month for comprehensive coverage that would cost $350 to $700 off-Marketplace. Employer plans are not subject to immigration eligibility rules. Off-Marketplace direct purchase is the alternative for self-employed DACA recipients or those without employer coverage who do not qualify for state programs. Full-premium Silver plans typically run $450 to $600 per month for an individual in 2026 with no federal subsidy. State-funded programs reduce this dramatically in New Mexico, Washington, Colorado, and New York. The decision matrix for choosing is: employer plan first (if available); state program second (if you are in California, New Mexico, Washington, New York, or Colorado and income-eligible); off-Marketplace direct purchase third (if income allows, no state program available); FQHC as a supplement or last resort for primary care, dental, and behavioral health when no coverage is accessible. FQHC care alone does not cover hospitalization or emergency surgery, so it is best used alongside minimal catastrophic coverage where possible.
body.es: Los receptores de DACA en 2026 tienen cuatro caminos de cobertura, cada uno con un perfil de costos muy diferente. Los planes del empleador son la opción más sólida: si su empleador ofrece seguro médico grupal, inscríbase de inmediato. Los empleadores típicamente cubren el 70 a 80 por ciento de la prima, haciendo que los costos de bolsillo sean $50 a $200 al mes. Los programas estatales reducen dramáticamente el costo de compra directa en Nuevo México, Washington, Colorado y Nueva York. La matriz de decisión es: plan del empleador primero; programa estatal segundo si está en California, Nuevo México, Washington, Nueva York o Colorado; compra directa fuera del Mercado tercero; FQHC como suplemento o último recurso para atención primaria cuando no hay cobertura accesible.

en.question: Can DACA recipients get health insurance through the ACA Marketplace in 2026?
en.answer: No. DACA recipients became permanently ineligible for ACA Marketplace plans, Premium Tax Credits, cost-sharing reductions, and the Basic Health Program effective August 25, 2025, under a final federal rule issued by the Trump administration in June 2025. DACA recipients enrolled before that date were disenrolled as of October 1, 2025, in states using HealthCare.gov. Attempting to enroll at HealthCare.gov will result in denial. The rule is not a temporary change and does not have a scheduled sunset date.

en.question: What health insurance options are available for DACA recipients in 2026?
en.answer: Four primary options remain for DACA recipients in 2026. First, employer-sponsored health insurance if your job offers group benefits, since private employers can cover employees regardless of immigration status. Second, off-Marketplace direct purchase from private insurers at full premium with no federal subsidy, costing roughly $350 to $700 per month for an individual. Third, Federally Qualified Health Centers providing primary care, dental, and behavioral health on a sliding-scale fee basis year-round with no eligibility barriers. Fourth, state-funded programs in New Mexico, Washington, New York, and Colorado that use state funds to extend some coverage to DACA residents outside the federal Marketplace framework.

en.question: Does losing Marketplace coverage trigger a Special Enrollment Period for employer plans?
en.answer: Yes. Losing qualifying health coverage is a qualifying life event under HIPAA Section 9831 for most employer group health plans. DACA recipients who lost Marketplace coverage on October 1, 2025 had approximately 30 days from that date to enroll in an available employer plan. If you missed that window, you must wait for your employer's next annual open enrollment period, typically November or December each year for January 1 plan year coverage. Contact your HR department immediately and request written documentation of the qualifying event enrollment window to ensure you are in the correct enrollment window for 2026 coverage.

en.question: What are Federally Qualified Health Centers and how do I access them?
en.answer: Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) are community health centers funded under the Health Center Program (42 U.S.C. Section 254b) that must serve all patients regardless of immigration status, insurance status, or ability to pay. There are over 1,400 FQHC organizations with more than 15,000 service sites in every state. Services include primary care, prenatal and pediatric care, dental, behavioral health, and pharmacy services. Fees are set on a sliding scale based on your household income relative to the 2026 Federal Poverty Level. Use the HRSA Find a Health Center tool at findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov to locate one near you. No immigration paperwork beyond identification is required to access care at an FQHC.

en.question: Does California Medi-Cal still cover DACA recipients in 2026?
en.answer: Medi-Cal continues to cover DACA recipients who were enrolled before January 1, 2026. However, new Medi-Cal enrollment for adults age 19 and older who are undocumented or have DACA status has been frozen as of January 1, 2026, due to California state budget constraints. DACA recipients who were not enrolled in Medi-Cal by December 31, 2025 cannot newly enroll under the same provisions as of early 2026. Check current eligibility rules directly at coveredca.com or your county social services office, as these rules may change with the state budget cycle.

en.question: What state has the clearest DACA-specific health insurance program in 2026?
en.answer: New Mexico has the most direct DACA-specific health coverage program in 2026. The New Mexico Health Care Authority offers a state-funded premium assistance program at hca.nm.gov/daca-coverage that provides a Clear Cost Gold Plan with income-based sliding scale premium assistance for DACA recipients living in New Mexico. Washington state also offers a strong option through Washington Healthplanfinder at wahbexchange.org, where DACA recipients can enroll using state-funded premium assistance that replaces the federal Premium Tax Credit. Both programs use income as a percentage of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level guidelines to determine assistance amounts.

en.question: Does the DACA court litigation change health insurance eligibility in 2026?
en.answer: No. The ongoing federal court litigation about the DACA program itself, including the Fifth Circuit's January 2025 ruling and its Texas-specific mandate, is legally separate from the 2025 Marketplace eligibility rule. The Marketplace exclusion is a separate administrative rule issued under ACA rulemaking authority and remains in effect regardless of how courts rule on the broader DACA program. DACA recipients can continue renewing their DACA status and EAD work authorization, but this renewed status does not restore Marketplace health insurance eligibility. The two legal issues are on separate tracks.

en.question: Can DACA recipients purchase health insurance directly from an insurer in 2026?
en.answer: Yes. DACA recipients can purchase health insurance directly from private insurance companies outside of the Marketplace exchange without any immigration status restriction. These off-Exchange Qualified Health Plans cover the same essential health benefits as Marketplace plans. The significant downside is cost: without a Premium Tax Credit, premiums run approximately $350 to $700 per month for an individual depending on age, location, and plan tier in 2026. Contact major insurers such as Blue Cross Blue Shield, Aetna, UnitedHealthcare, or Cigna directly or use an independent insurance broker to compare off-Exchange plans in your area.

es.question: ¿Pueden los receptores de DACA obtener seguro médico a través del Mercado ACA en 2026?
es.answer: No. Los receptores de DACA quedaron permanentemente inelegibles para planes del Mercado ACA, Créditos Fiscales de Prima, reducciones de costos compartidos y el Programa Básico de Salud desde el 25 de agosto de 2025, bajo una regla federal final emitida por la administración Trump en junio de 2025. Los receptores de DACA inscritos antes de esa fecha fueron dados de baja al 1 de octubre de 2025 en estados que usan HealthCare.gov. La regla no es un cambio temporal y no tiene fecha de vencimiento programada.

es.question: ¿Qué opciones de seguro médico están disponibles para los receptores de DACA en 2026?
es.answer: Quedan cuatro opciones principales para los receptores de DACA en 2026. Primera, seguro médico del empleador si su trabajo ofrece beneficios grupales, ya que los empleadores privados pueden cubrir a los empleados independientemente del estatus migratorio. Segunda, compra directa fuera del Mercado de aseguradoras privadas a prima completa sin subsidio federal, costando aproximadamente $350 a $700 al mes para un individuo. Tercera, Centros de Salud Comunitaria Federalmente Calificados que brindan atención primaria, dental y salud conductual en una escala de tarifas según ingreso durante todo el año. Cuarta, programas estatales en Nuevo México, Washington, Nueva York y Colorado.

es.question: ¿Perder la cobertura del Mercado activa un Período de Inscripción Especial para planes del empleador?
es.answer: Sí. Perder cobertura de salud calificada es un evento calificador de vida bajo HIPAA Sección 9831 para la mayoría de los planes grupales del empleador. Los receptores de DACA que perdieron la cobertura del Mercado el 1 de octubre de 2025 tuvieron aproximadamente 30 días desde esa fecha para inscribirse en un plan del empleador disponible. Si perdió esa ventana, debe esperar el próximo período de inscripción abierta anual de su empleador, típicamente noviembre o diciembre para cobertura del 1 de enero.

es.question: ¿Qué son los Centros de Salud Comunitaria Federalmente Calificados y cómo accedo a ellos?
es.answer: Los Centros de Salud Comunitaria Federalmente Calificados (FQHC) son centros de salud comunitaria financiados bajo el Programa de Centros de Salud (42 U.S.C. Sección 254b) que deben atender a todos los pacientes independientemente del estatus migratorio, de seguro o capacidad de pago. Hay más de 1,400 organizaciones FQHC con más de 15,000 sitios de servicio en todos los estados. Los servicios incluyen atención primaria, prenatal y pediátrica, dental, salud conductual y farmacia. Use la herramienta HRSA en findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov para localizar uno cerca de usted.

es.question: ¿California Medi-Cal todavía cubre a los receptores de DACA en 2026?
es.answer: Medi-Cal continúa cubriendo a los receptores de DACA que estaban inscritos antes del 1 de enero de 2026. Sin embargo, la nueva inscripción en Medi-Cal para adultos de 19 años o más con estatus DACA fue congelada desde el 1 de enero de 2026 por restricciones presupuestarias del estado de California. Los receptores de DACA que no estaban inscritos en Medi-Cal antes del 31 de diciembre de 2025 no pueden inscribirse nuevamente bajo las mismas disposiciones. Verifique las reglas de elegibilidad actuales en coveredca.com o en su oficina de servicios sociales del condado.

es.question: ¿Qué estado tiene el programa de seguro médico específico para DACA más claro en 2026?
es.answer: Nuevo México tiene el programa de cobertura específica para DACA más directo en 2026. La Autoridad de Cuidado de Salud de Nuevo México ofrece un programa de asistencia premium estatal en hca.nm.gov/daca-coverage que proporciona un Plan Clear Cost Gold con asistencia premium según ingreso para receptores de DACA residentes en Nuevo México. Washington también ofrece una opción sólida a través de Washington Healthplanfinder en wahbexchange.org, donde los receptores de DACA pueden inscribirse usando asistencia premium estatal que reemplaza el Crédito Fiscal de Prima federal.

es.question: ¿El litigio judicial sobre DACA cambia la elegibilidad de seguro médico en 2026?
es.answer: No. El litigio federal en curso sobre el programa DACA, incluyendo el fallo del Quinto Circuito de enero de 2025, es legalmente separado de la regla de elegibilidad del Mercado de 2025. La exclusión del Mercado es una regla administrativa separada emitida bajo la autoridad de elaboración de reglas del ACA y permanece en vigor. Los receptores de DACA pueden continuar renovando su estatus DACA y autorización de trabajo EAD, pero este estatus renovado no restaura la elegibilidad de seguro médico del Mercado.

es.question: ¿Pueden los receptores de DACA comprar seguro médico directamente de una aseguradora en 2026?
es.answer: Sí. Los receptores de DACA pueden comprar seguro médico directamente de compañías de seguros privadas fuera del Mercado sin ninguna restricción de estatus migratorio. Estos Planes de Salud Calificados fuera del Mercado cubren los mismos beneficios esenciales de salud. La desventaja significativa es el costo: sin un Crédito Fiscal de Prima, las primas son aproximadamente $350 a $700 al mes para un individuo dependiendo de la edad, ubicación y nivel del plan en 2026. Contacte directamente a aseguradoras principales como Blue Cross Blue Shield, Aetna, UnitedHealthcare o Cigna, o use un corredor de seguros independiente.
